chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman from Ibn Muskhan from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"Prayer during travel is two rak'ahs; there is nothing before them or after them except for Maghrib, for after it are four rak'ahs; do not leave them in residence or in travel. And there is no making up for you the prayer of the day, and pray the prayer of the night and make it up."

The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And one who completes (the prayer) in travel out of forgetfulness, he repeats it if the time remains, and if the time has passed, there is no repetition upon him. And whoever intentionally completes in travel after the one who has the right of argument (the Imam) upon him being in shortening, that does not suffice him and repetition becomes obligatory upon him.
ai.seo_question: What are the rules for shortening and completing prayers during travel in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the baseline for travel prayers (qasr) as two rak'ahs, while uniquely mandating four rak'ahs for Maghrib regardless of location, a ruling emphasized by the phrase 'do not leave them.' Shaykh al-Tusi adds a crucial jurisprudential distinction: if one intentionally performs four rak'ahs during travel after the era of the Imams, the prayer is valid but not fully sufficient (laa juzi), requiring repetition, whereas unintentional errors are excused if the time remains. This highlights the Shia emphasis on both the legal technicality of qasr and the spiritual discipline of maintaining night prayers (salat al-layl) even when making up daytime misses.
